page: Microsoft Azure M176bs_v3 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the MBSMediumMemoryv3 family. It features 176 dedicated vCPUs derived from 88 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8473C processor running at 4.0 GHz. The processor includes a 105 MB L3 cache and supports Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The system is equipped with 1536.0 GB of RAM, providing approximately 8.73 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, relying instead on external block storage.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores placing in the top 10% of tested servers. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with both small-block cached read speeds and large-block uncached read/write speeds ranking in the top 10%. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core results falling in the middle 50%, though Geekbench single-core scores reach the top 10%. The server demonstrates strong capabilities in database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput, all of which rank in the top 10%.

From a resource density perspective, the M176bs_v3 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require local NVMe storage. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached block storage, which may introduce latency tradeoffs depending on the storage tier selected. Given its high memory capacity and strong multi-threaded decompression and database benchmark results, this server is suited for large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching platforms like Redis, software compilation, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks.
